title: A fibration with a point, a decoding map and two equations makes the loop space equivalent to the fibre at the base point
author: The Univalent Foundations Program

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 2571-2582: under a fibration with a point of the fibre at the base point, a decoding map and two equations, the loop space at the base point is equivalent to that fibre. The proof (source lines 2584-2600) is not a pointer: it defines the encoding map as transport of the given point along the path, then exhibits the decoding map as its two-sided inverse. One round trip is exactly one of the two hypotheses, and the other is stated pointwise for every path out of the base point and reduced by path induction to a single identity at the base point, where the transport computes and the second hypothesis applies. The definition of the encoding map and the reduction of the second round trip are the substance, and the statement alone does not display them.
